title: Shake Hands with the Devil: The Failure of Humanity in Rwanda
author: Roméo Dallaire (with Major Brent Beardsley)
edition_analyzed: First edition (published by Random House Canada, 2003)
target_audience: Readers interested in modern history and genocide studies
Students and scholars of international relations and peacekeeping
Military professionals and those studying international conflict
Human rights advocates and policy makers
General readers seeking a firsthand account of the Rwandan genocide
core_themes: Genocide and the limits of international intervention
Moral responsibility and the psychological cost of failure
The failings of the United Nations and world powers
The complexity of leadership in crisis
primary_purpose: To give a personal, unflinching account of Roméo Dallaire's experiences as the Force Commander of the United Nations Assistance Mission for Rwanda (UNAMIR) during the 1994 genocide, exposing the apathy of the international community and offering insight into the mechanisms and failures that allowed mass murder to occur.

structure_format.narrative_style: First-person, chronological memoir interspersed with analysis and reflection
structure_format.organization: Divided into three major parts—prelude to genocide, the genocide, and its aftermath—with short, thematic chapters within each section
features: Personal anecdotes and detailed daily accounts
Reflections on psychological trauma and ethical dilemmas

key_concepts_lessons: International peacekeeping missions are severely hampered without clear mandates and adequate resources.
Leadership demands both moral courage and operational clarity under extreme human and political stress.
Bureaucratic inertia, political self-interest, and racism hinder effective intervention in humanitarian crises.
Bearing witness to atrocity comes with profound personal and psychological consequences.
The world must reckon with its failures to prevent genocide to learn and improve future responses.
notable_features: Firsthand perspective of the highest-ranking UN officer during the Rwandan genocide
Detailed examination of UN operations and failures
Raw descriptions of violence, bureaucratic obstacles, and personal trauma
Widely used in university courses on genocide, peacekeeping, and international policy
cultural_historical_context: Written by the Canadian general who led UNAMIR, the book was published at a time when global reflection on humanitarian intervention, international law, and United Nations reform was intensifying. The Rwandan genocide (1994) was a watershed moment, highlighting the catastrophic consequences of global inaction.
reception_impact: Winner of the Governor General's Award for Non-Fiction (Canada)
Acclaimed for its honesty, depth, and contribution to the history of the Rwandan genocide
Inspired a documentary film and a dramatic feature film adaptation
Frequently cited in discussions of peacekeeping reform and the moral imperatives of intervention
Praised for raising awareness but also criticized for graphic descriptions and emotional toll

A Problem from Hell: America and the Age of Genocide by Samantha Power
